e: Pakaraka School became the first state school in New Zealand to convert to a charter school.
Firefighters contain the vegetation fire near Lake Wakatipu. The fire had devastated 1,350 hectares of tussock and scrubland over a three day period.

The New Zealand Crown decides not to seek a retrial against David Tamihere, whose convictions for the Murder of Urban Höglin and Heidi Paakkonen were quashed by the Supreme Court of New Zealand in February 2026.

A vegetation fire on the southern shores of Lake Wakatipu has spread to cover 1,200 hectares due to strong winds and dry conditions. Firefighters and helicopters carrying monsoon buckets are deployed.
A large vegetation wildfire breaks out on the southern shores of Lake Wakatipu in the early hours of the morning, fanned by strong winds.
The New Zealand Government and local government bodies sign the Otago Central Lakes Deal, a ten-year plan to improve infrastructure and healthcare in Central Otago.
Name suppression is lifted for Private Jack Captein, the former New Zealand Army soldier who was convicted in August 2025 of attempted espionage.

A pod of pygmy killer whales become stranded on Ninety Mile Beach in the Far North District. By the following day, at least 12 to 15 whales have died despite efforts by volunteers, iwi and conservation staff to refloat them.

The Greater Wellington Regional Council files criminal charges against both the Wellington City Council and water services provider Tiaki Wai over their handling of the Moa Point wastewater spillage in February 2026.
The 54th New Zealand Parliament is formally dissolved.

Four new road rules allowing children to ride bicycles on footpaths, e-scooters to use cycle lanes, requiring drivers to give way to buses exiting bus stops, and motorists to give cyclists, horse riders and other road users a 1.5 metre passing gap come into effect.

Dutch environmentalist group Both ENDS files a complaint against New Zealand with the European Commission for allegedly breaching the climate change provisions of the EU–NZ free trade agreement. The group's complaint was supported by several New Zealand groups and individuals including Greenpeace New Zealand, the Environmental Law Initiative, Mike Smith and University of Auckland law Professor Jane Kelsey.
Woolworths New Zealand confirms plans to cut 130 customer care jobs in Auckland in order to centralise customer care operations in Sydney.
The Auckland Council votes to shift from postal voting to in-person voting at the 2028 New Zealand local elections.
The Waitangi Tribunal finds that the New Zealand Crown had failed to develop an alternative Māori health plan after it dissolved Te Aka Whai Ora (the Māori Health Authority) in late February 2024.
The Government pauses making decisions on its local government reforms until after the 2026 New Zealand general election.
A fast-track approvals panel rejects mining company Bathurst Resources's application to mine Denniston Plateau on the West Coast Region.

Gloriavale Christian Community's charitable arm is stripped of its charitable status by the Charities Registration Board due to "serious wrongdoing" including the use of child labour and failing to report sexual crime.
Parliament passes the Planning and Natural Environment Acts replacing the Resource Management Act 1991 as the country's main legislative framework for infrastructural and environmental regulations.

An independent review commissioned by the Government found that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand was too slow to raise interest rates during the COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, resulting in record high inflation.
The black robin is named Bird of the Year.
Parliament passes legislation easing earthquake strengthening rules in most of New Zealand, including the upper North Island and the Chatham Islands.
Thousands of protestors opposed to the Government's proposed Conservation Amendment legislation march through Auckland.
Parliament passes legislation empowering Police to issue "move-on" orders in response to begging, rough sleeping, disorderly behaviour and obstructing businesses.
Parliament passes two separate laws implementing the New Zealand–India Free Trade Agreement and empowering the Youth Court of New Zealand to send youth offenders to Military Style Academies.

Prime Minister Luxon apologises to the children of the fugitive father Tom Phillips and their mother Cat after an inquiry identified serious shortcomings in the responses of several government agencies including the New Zealand Police and Oranga Tamariki in preventing the children's disappearance and rescuing them.
Parliament passes legislation directing local government bodies to focus on delivering core services and limiting council voting to elected members.
Auckland's City Rail Link opens to the public.
Richard Naish is awarded the NZIA Gold Medal for 2026.
Public servants affiliated with the Public Service Association strike nationwide to protest against the Government's proposed public sector job cuts and to demand inflation-adjusted pay rises.
The New Zealand Parliament passes legislation tightening the welfare benefits criteria for teenagers aged 18 and 19-years old based on a parental income test.
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand increases the official cash rate by 25 basis points to 2.75%.
State pharmaceutical provider Pharmac makes flu vaccines for children under five years old free in response to rising flu cases nationwide.
The New Zealand government delays plans to raise fuel excise taxes until 2028.

A historic meeting of the leaders of the four constituent members of the Realm of New Zealand to discuss constitutional arrangements is held in Auckland. This meeting is attended by Prime Minister Luxon, Ulu-o-Tokelau Alapati Tavite, Niue Prime Minister Dalton Tagelagi, and Cook Islands Prime Minister Mark Brown.
Heavy rain overnight leads to flooding in Queenstown, resulting in the evacuation of 45 residents.

The National-led coalition government introduces legislation into Parliament to ban people under the age of 16 from accessing social media. The coalition ACT New Zealand and New Zealand First parties express disagreement with the proposed law.
Strong winds cause power outages and travel disruptions across both the North and South Islands.
A wildfire near Albert Town leads to the evacuation of 22 homes.

A by-election triggered by the death of Greater Wellington Regional Council deputy chairperson and Wairarapa constituency councillor Adrienne Staples is held. Independent candidate John Hart wins the by-election.
